column1: # The national ID numbers private mode knows (ADR-0062). One row per scheme, four tab-separated
# fields: key, tesseract language(s), residue shape, plain words.
# - A profile's private-mode line names the person's schemes with ⟨id-scheme KEY⟩, several as
#   ⟨id-scheme KEY,KEY⟩. A line without the exact tag reads as EVERY row here (ADR-0077). The key
#   `unlisted` is reserved: a number not on the list, covered by hand; no row may use it.
# - The residue shape is what guard L10 and its Python companions red in a marked person's derived
#   text. Write it as a POSIX extended regular expression that Python reads the same way: bracket
#   ranges such as [0-9], no [[:digit:]] classes, no lookaround, a tab written \t and no other
#   backslash (L10 receives a real tab). Bound a shape with
#   (^|[^0-9A-Fa-f]) and ([^0-9A-Fa-f]|$) so it matches neither inside a longer number nor inside a
#   hash or a `doc-` folder name. Where a bare run looks like a phone or a barcode, search only the
#   separated or keyed forms: the masking tool still masks the bare one on the page. The first row
#   keeps the shape it always had.
# - A tag is read strictly (ADR-0073): on the marker line a mistyped tag is refused, never read as absent.
# - Never write a scheme's local name or a printed label here: an instance may list its own as a firewall token.

column4: the US nine-digit personal taxpayer number
